data.long_meaning: Hashit is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'ashva', which means 'horse' or 'vehicle'. In Hindu mythology, Hashit is the name of a celestial horse, the mount of the Sun God Surya. This name symbolizes power, strength, and swiftness. The name Hashit carries the meaning “Horse, Vehicle” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Hashit usually hope their child will grow to embody horse, vehicle and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Hashit was a legendary king of the Haihayas, a dynasty ruling parts of present-day Bihar and Nepal. He is known for his victory over the Shakas, an invading tribe from Central Asia. Hashit's rule is believed to have been around 500 BC.
Hashit is also mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, as the father of Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Pandava and Kaurava princes. This reference does not specify a particular time period.
